justification: Standard: changes which applicability entry a parts-council row takes, a hard filter on what a property is shown. Measured by dry run to move only Woollahra D5's 16 served rows; nothing is written to production by this PR.

pre_impl.existing_data: Woollahra served rows: 13 on no_config whose document names a configured chapter (DQ-126). Parts councils in scope: woollahra, waverley, northern_beaches, parramatta, dry-run against production 2026-10-04.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The parts path assumed a heading's section code names the row's chapter. Woollahra D5 numbers its own sections A1.x and A2.x, so its rows looked up A2 (repealed, no entry) or took chapter A1's scope.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends the existing document_id fallback in _get_config_driven instead of adding a new path; the same regex chapter_([a-z]\d+) now also overrides a heading code from a different chapter.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_probe_app_defects.py --id DQ-126 (after the retag) ; pytest tests/enrichment/test_applicability_tagger.py -k Woollahra
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Reads 13 now and stays above 0 if the retag runs with the old tagger; the Woollahra tests fail when the override is removed (3 fail) or the subsection test loses its dot boundary (1 fails).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: DQ-126 = 13 on 2026-10-04 (exit 1); mutation removing the override: 3 failed; mutation dropping the '.' boundary: 1 failed.

functions.name: ApplicabilityTagger._get_config_driven (parts path)
functions.input: document_id and provision_text of a regulatory_provisions row for a parts council
functions.output: the config entry of the chapter the document names when the heading code belongs to another chapter
functions.if_none: no document chapter code: the heading code is used exactly as before; neither present: returns None (no_config)

break_it.scenario: A heading code that only shares a prefix with the chapter, e.g. D12 inside chapter D1
break_it.what_happens: A plain startswith check would keep D12 and read the wrong chapter's entry
break_it.how: subsection test requires the chapter code followed by a dot (D1.x), else the document wins
break_it.repro: pytest test_a_code_that_only_shares_a_prefix_is_a_different_chapter; mutation without the dot fails it

break_it.scenario: A council whose documents carry no chapter_ code (Parramatta numbered parts, Warringah full DCP)
break_it.what_happens: Any change there could hide controls through the zero-default numeric parts hazard
break_it.how: the override only fires when document_id matches chapter_<letter><digit>; dry runs for those councils are byte-identical
break_it.repro: retag dry run --councils parramatta / northern_beaches / waverley diffed against the unchanged tagger: no differences

break_it.scenario: Rows moved onto D5's entry are narrowed from ALL zones to E1
break_it.what_happens: A narrowing can hide a control from a property outside the centre if the scope were wrong
break_it.how: E1 is D5's own recorded scope with verbatim evidence (D5.1.1); the retag requires --expect-narrowings 16 exactly and backs up every row
break_it.repro: dry run lists 16 narrowings, all chapter_d5_double_bay_centre, one shape ['ALL'] -> ['E1']

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- with the user's go, from a worktree at merged origin/main: python scripts/retag_applicability_slug_docids.py --councils woollahra --apply --expect-narrowings 16, then DQ-126 should read 0.
